dedupe_keys.name: impacc evaluation of a redesigned 9 1 1 paramedic model of care for lower acuity patients canada

description: This case study evaluates IMPACC, a model of care that widens what paramedics can do for patients who call 9-1-1 with lower-acuity or undifferentiated problems, instead of defaulting to transport to hospital. The authors, led by Walter Tavares with colleagues from Unity Health Toronto, the University Health Network, Lakeridge Health, Queen's University, Dalhousie University and other institutions, embedded IMPACC in an existing 9-1-1 system and ran a retrospective cohort study of 7,382 encounters attended by IMPACC-trained paramedics from April 2024 to February 2026, with an exact-matched comparison against standard practice. The article was published in Prehospital Emergency Care in September 2026, with an author copy free to read online on figshare. Coverage is one paramedic service in Canada, the country of all the authors' institutions. Caveats: the study is observational, and the service's data are not public. IMPACC was activated in 9.9 percent of encounters, 12.6 percent among lower-acuity triage levels and 28.3 percent among the most active quarter of paramedics, mostly for clinically ambiguous complaints, and activated encounters had lower hospital transport. Simulation uses: pathway shares and dispositions for paramedic demand, conveyance and emergency department inflow models. Related records: the 9-1-1 language barrier data (data-icpsr-911-language-barriers-dispatch-outcomes) and the Region Zealand dispatch trends (case_study-region-zealand-ambulance-dispatch-response-time-trends) concern related services.
